children: Shares of Viking Therapeutics jumped after the company disclosed what it called positive top-line results from a maintenance study of its weight-loss drug.
The stock rose 39%, to $41.85, in premarket trading Tuesday. Through Monday's close, shares were down 14% year to date.

The biopharmaceutical company said before the bell that patients in the study who received its treatment, VK2735, demonstrated superior weight maintenance following the transition to less frequent dosing regimens, compared with subjects who transitioned to placebo.

The treatment--a dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide 1, or GLP-1, and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, or GIP, receptors--additionally demonstrated an encouraging safety and tolerability profile, the company added.

"We believe this dose-ranging study clearly demonstrated the potential viability of novel, extended dosing approaches for maintenance," Viking Therapeutics CEO Brian Lian said. "We believe flexible dosing approaches will provide both patients and their providers with new options for improving long-term adherence to therapy and sustained weight management."
